facts.text: Taiwan's high-speed rail began carrying passengers in January 2007.
The line runs about 345 km along Taiwan's west coast, from Taipei in the north to Kaohsiung in the south.
In 2007, an express high-speed train with one stop in between took about 90 minutes from Taipei to Kaohsiung; a train stopping at seven stations took about two hours.
facts.note: 2007 年（Wharton 2007 年 9 月報導當時）的情形，不是現況，選文不可用 now 或現在式寫成現在的事實。2026 年的直達車在台北與左營之間至少停 2 站（板橋＋台中，或板橋＋台南），最快的台北－左營約 95 分鐘（2026 年 2 月新增的 1985 車次；ai.rd.7fd13e 的 fact_check 意見，本事實單沒有收錄 2026 年時刻表的來源）

facts.text: Before the high-speed rail, the trip from Taipei to Kaohsiung took about five hours by regular train or by express bus.
High-speed trains reach almost 300 km per hour between stations.
In the high-speed rail's first year, some domestic air routes lost more than half of their passengers, and airlines canceled dozens of flights.
In 2015, some high-speed trains began stopping at new stations in Miaoli, Changhua and Yunlin counties.
In 2020, the high-speed rail ran fewer trains for a time because the COVID-19 pandemic had reduced the number of travelers.
On May 19, 2021, Taiwan raised its COVID-19 alert to level 3 nationwide, and high-speed rail ridership dropped sharply.
Ridership in 2023 reached a record because rail travel bounced back strongly after pandemic rules were relaxed.
Yearly passengers (data.gov.tw): 15.56 million in 2007, 30.58 million in 2008, 67.41 million in 2019, 43.46 million in 2021, 73.09 million in 2023 and 82.07 million in 2025.
The 2008 total (30.58 million) was almost twice the 2007 total (15.56 million).
The 2025 total (82.07 million) was more than five times the 2007 total (15.56 million) and was the highest of any year up to 2025.
Yearly passengers first went above 60 million in 2017 (60.57 million); the 2016 total was 56.59 million.
During 2007 the number of daily trains kept rising, from 19 at the opening to 46 by mid-September.
